# AudioSceneVolume <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [BlitzBasic](BlitzBasic) · [Audio](BlitzBasic-Audio)

</div>


```blitzbasic
AudioSceneVolume:Void scene:Int32, bus:Int32, volume:Float32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scene` | In | Int32 | required | A scene from [CreateAudioScene](CreateAudioScene). Anything else is a runtime error. |
| `bus` | In | Int32 | required | A bus from [CreateAudioBus](CreateAudioBus), or `0` for the master bus. Anything else is a runtime error. |
| `volume` | In | Float32 | required | As for [AudioBusVolume](AudioBusVolume). Below 0 is a runtime error. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Sets the volume that a bus gets when the scene is applied. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

## Differences

* When a bus is freed, every scene forgets its volume, so an old scene never changes the bus that gets the same handle later.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
AudioSceneVolume paused, world, 0.2
```
